answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Each submission hangs on the inlet of a task receipt, and the falcon is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, released only after three unrelated confirmations, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. The prism of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short.
